clue.text: Part of ship in port

definitions.meaning: the main body or shell of a vessel
Kingston upon ..., a major English port on the Humber

explanation.surface: A puzzle about naming a ship's component found in a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: HULL is the formal short name of a port city in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Two separate senses: the watertight body of a vessel, and the name of an English harbour city.

clue.text: Hard gospel for everyone to penetrate — a distinctive feature

indicators.note: the phrase for everyone goes into the middle of the hard-plus-gospel pair

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
Mark is one of the four Gospels
for everyone means for all

explanation.surface: A preacher hopes a tough gospel message will get through to everyone, as a signature trait.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic mark that identifies something, originally the assay stamp on precious metal.

clue.text: Drink in article in French paper

indicators.note: the article sits inside the name of the newspaper

parts.note: Le Monde is a leading French daily newspaper
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone reads about a beverage in a French newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article in French' looks like LE, but the French is part of the newspaper's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft beverage made with lemons, sugar and water, often fizzy in Britain.

clue.text: Fresh fighting force to include fellow shopkeepers

parts.note: fresh means new

indicators.note: the fighting force's letters wrap around the word for fellow

parts.note: the SAS is the British Special Air Service regiment
a gent is a fellow or man

explanation.surface: A new army unit recruits a man who runs shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who run shops selling papers and magazines, so a kind of retailer.

clue.text: This person turned up and encountered an insect

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: this person is the setter, me
encountered means met

explanation.surface: Someone arrived and met a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: An old dialect word for an ant, a small social insect.

clue.text: One observes holy group keeping quiet on a hill

indicators.note: the holy group holds the quiet letter inside it

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone watches a religious community keeping silent on a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher at an event, someone looking on rather than taking part.

clue.text: Fulfil two functions on Christmas Day as concession?

definitions.text: Fulfil two functions on Christmas Day
definitions.meaning: on Christmas Day people both hand out and receive presents
mutual compromise, each side yielding something

explanation.surface: Christmas gift-swapping as a model of compromise.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful literal reading of the phrase: giving and receiving presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutual compromise where each party yields something to the other, an idiom for concession.

clue.text: Politician from Newcastle area with old trick

parts.note: Newcastle is in the North East of England, NE
a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A Geordie politician with a long-established scam.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for neoconservative, a right-wing politician favouring assertive foreign policy.

clue.text: Notice little boy hiding in that plant

indicators.note: the word for notice conceals the boy's name within it

parts.note: to notice is to see
Sam is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: Spot the young lad hiding behind that shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual herb grown for its oil-rich seeds, used in cooking.

clue.text: Weak lover, female dumped

indicators.note: the abbreviation for female is thrown out of the word for lover

parts.note: an old flame is a former lover

explanation.surface: A feeble boyfriend has been dropped by his girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble or unconvincing, as in a poor excuse.

clue.text: High-handed, inwardly very resistant

indicators.note: the abbreviation for very is placed within the word for high-handed

parts.note: imperious means arrogant and domineering

explanation.surface: An arrogant person is, deep down, very stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaffected by or not allowing something through, hence able to withstand.

clue.text: Beware of clique showing established attitudes

parts.note: mind, as in 'mind the gap', means beware of
a set is a social group or clique

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out for a cliquey group with fixed views.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed way of thinking, a habitual set of opinions or outlook.

clue.text: Careerist worked a short time in admin department

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An ambitious careerist put in a brief stint in the office administration.
explanation.definitionFit: The administrative office of an organisation, staffed by its officials and clerks.

clue.text: Little Aussie beast interrupting side in cafe

indicators.note: the animal breaks into the middle of the word for side

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
roo is the clipped Australian word for a kangaroo

explanation.surface: A small kangaroo bursts into a café and disrupts a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: A small restaurant serving tea and light refreshments, a kind of café.

clue.text: Nasty red coat covered in grass? Should be smartened up again!

indicators.note: the reworked coat letters are enclosed by the word for grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: a nasty coat is a bad one, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A grubby red coat lying in the grass needs smartening up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful idea of grass decorating a coat; the anagram of the coat letters gives DECORAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Repainted or refurbished, given a fresh decorative treatment once more.

clue.text: Memory of number in Orient being tortured

indicators.note: the number goes inside the reworked letters of Orient
tortured means twisted out of shape

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone recalls numbers while being tortured in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orient' looks like the East in the surface, but it is only fodder; 'being tortured' rearranges its six letters to RETION.
explanation.definitionFit: The faculty of keeping information in mind, the power to recall.

clue.text: Fashionable Oxford feature, Oxford ultimately being wonderful

parts.note: in means fashionable
Oxford is the city of dreaming spires

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the second Oxford

explanation.surface: A trendy Oxford building that ultimately looks marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: Of outstanding quality, as if divinely prompted, hence brilliant.

clue.text: Men starting off in stages to provide small bombs

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the word for stages

parts.note: grades are stages or levels

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off the word Men

explanation.surface: Soldiers are issued with explosives in phases.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand-thrown explosive devices, bombs small enough to throw.

clue.text: One looking for applause has to come in and earn it possibly

parts.note: to come in is to enter

indicators.note: possibly says the letters might take another arrangement

explanation.surface: A performer has to walk on stage and win the clapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer such as a comedian or singer, who seeks the audience's clapping.

clue.text: In workplace I love being led by boss

indicators.note: the following letters come after the word for boss

parts.note: a stud or boss is a raised knob or ornament
love is zero in tennis, like the letter O

explanation.surface: An employee loves working under their boss.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or photographer's working room, or a broadcasting room.

clue.text: Bird is pinned by something pointed — not good

indicators.note: the word is is held fast inside the pointed object
the abbreviation for good is removed

parts.note: a prong is a pointed tine of a fork

explanation.surface: A bird is skewered on a sharp spike, which is bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a jail sentence or jail itself, from rhyming slang 'birdlime' = time.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: doing bird means serving time in jail.

clue.text: Ground swamped by winter rains

indicators.note: the letters are submerged within the run of words winter rains

explanation.surface: Land flooded by the winter downpours.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of land considered for its physical features.

clue.text: Revolutionary, a writer in disgrace

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A rebel and an author caught up in scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: To degrade or lower the dignity of someone, a verb meaning to shame.

clue.text: Utter confusion when Charles admits love

indicators.note: the short name lets the letter in, holding it inside

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Things go haywire when Charles confesses his feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Total disorder, a state of complete pandemonium.

clue.text: With sun coming in, mild air is somehow different

indicators.note: the sun's abbreviation enters the reworked letters
somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: Sunshine arrives and the gentle weather changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' turns MILD AIR IS into DISIMILAR, and 'coming in' puts S among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Not alike, unlike one another, so differing.

clue.text: Walked and finally sat on perch

indicators.note: finally selects the closing letter of the word sat

parts.note: a perch is an old unit of length, the same as a rod or pole

explanation.surface: A bird walked about and at last settled on a perch.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of tread, to step or walk on something.

clue.text: Pomposity of earnest son spouting

indicators.note: spouting suggests the letters gushing out in disorder

explanation.surface: A serious young man's pompous ranting.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate, over-decorated style in language, hence a grand or pompous manner.

clue.text: Evens maybe — or maybe not

definitions.meaning: evens is one example of betting prices, which bookmakers quote
numbers that are not even are the uneven ones, one, three, five

explanation.surface: A shrug over whether something is fifty-fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: Evens is a betting price; the second reading is the plural of the uneven numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting prices such as evens, and as a plural noun, numbers not divisible by two.
